catalog_locator: sec. 5 'Tonal system' (MS pp. 9-10) and sec. 5.2.2 'Neutral tone syllables' (MS pp. 14-15); also sec. 5.2.3 (MS p. 16)
catalog_quote: Duoxu has four contrastive lexical tones on monosyllabic words, three tonal patterns on disyllabic words with the root /ə˞/ in second-syllable position (which are slightly longer than monosyllabic words), 15 tonal patterns on regular disyllabic domains (words and phrases), and neutral tone (or weak stress). ... Any citation monosyllabic word belongs to one of four contrastive tones. In the five-scale pitch system developed by Yuen Ren Chao (1930), these tones may be annotated as 53, 33, 22, and 31. ... Duoxu neutral tone syllables (without tonal marking in transcriptions) include clitics (such as the perfective marker /la/, the genitive marker /i/), reduplicated forms (e.g. /to⁵³-to/ 'hold, carry in the arms'), classifiers in disyllabic nouns consisting of a nominal root and a classifier (e.g. /Ndʑa⁵³-pu/ 'door'), and possibly, also the nominal affix -ma (as in /dje⁵⁵ma/ 'buttocks'). audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Chirkova 2015 phonological sketch at the stated sections/pages. The source is a dedicated phonology paper with acoustic measurements by the language's principal documenter; the classification 'tonal' (four lexical tones, neutral tone = 'weak stress' as a morphologically defined toneless class, no independent word-stress rule) is exactly what it says. Two further open Chirkova works fetched sources now (LTBA 2014; HDR 2020) restate the four-tone analysis, and the 2020 HDR explicitly types Duoxu as an omnisyllabic tone system in contrast to the tone-plus-accent systems of Lizu/Ersu, so nothing suggests the coding would change. The only superior description is the 2020 Commercial Press grammar co-authored by Chirkova (print only, Chinese); worth holding for completeness and for the >2-syllable domain, but not expected to alter the record. sources.quote: Duoxu 'possede un systeme du type omnisyllabique, avec un ton pour chaque syllabe', contrasted with the hybrid tone-and-accent systems of Lizu and Ersu; 'quatre tons lexicaux contrastifs sur les mots monosyllabiques ... 15 combinaisons de tons sur des domaines disyllabiques reguliers ... y compris des combinaisons comprenant un ton neutre'; tones 53, 31, 33, 22.
